entries.name: Warding
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies g.armour existingFamilies). channel/op taken directly from atom-family-library.md §3.1's table row (`warding | defense Flat | S | both`). `roles: ["standard"]` is not a narrowing choice, it is the entire point of the family: atom-family-library.md §4.1a / gap G8 shows primary `defense` reaches the lawn through one side-wide cached value in the `TakeDamage` prefix, never per-entity, so a `warding` atom on any body role silently does nothing for that body. classes.v1.json's `standard` implicit slate and `slateNote` name exactly this reasoning and exclude the family from every other slate for the same cause. `side: "both"` and `frames` cover both bodies because the defense channel itself is side-agnostic (atom-family-library.md §4.1: 'the whole resistance and shield mechanism belongs to both sides') — only the two vanilla arm1/arm2 fields are zombie-restricted, not this channel. No shipped word table exists for `warding` in ssot-affixes.md's illustrative §4.12 sample (only `plating` appears there for this group), so `nameWords` is minted here, drawing on the banner's own growing-hedge fiction rather than generic fantasy words.

entries.name: Resilience
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% increased defense for the whole army
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. channel/op from atom-family-library.md §3.1 (`resilience | defense Increased | S | both`) — the Increased sibling of `warding`, the same split as `vitality`/`fortitude` and `might`/`ferocity` on the primary side. Same G8 reasoning as `warding` restricts `roles` to `["standard"]`; ssot-affixes.md §4.7's worked example (`atom.resilience.t3`, +64‰ defense, bound at match) is the one place this family is shown actually resolving, and it is bound at `match` scope exactly as this file assumes. `powerBand: "low"` against `warding`'s `medium` mirrors the relative-pull judgement `atom.elpw-amplify` makes against `atom.elemental-power` in the affix-family exemplar — the ratio sibling sits below the flat one. No shipped word table exists for this family either; minted fresh, escalating from a weathered hide to true ironbark toughness.

entries.name: Plating
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. atom-family-library.md §3.1 lists this family's channel as `arm1 / arm1Max` and §4.1 confirms the field is zombie-only by engine fact, not by design. definitions.md §1 explains `variant` carries 'the channel for families like `plating` that write two channels', but no `variants.generate` vocabulary for a channel-pair exists anywhere in seed-contract.md or the exemplars — only `elements+omni` is documented there. Rather than invent an ungoverned generator instruction, this entry authors the single, unambiguous capacity channel `arm1Max` with `op: Flat`, mirroring `vitality`'s own `maxHp` Flat choice (the primary side already keeps current vs. capacity as separate levers via `mending` vs. `vitality`). Whether the executor also tops up current `arm1` to match is a generator/runtime concern, not an authored one — flagged here rather than guessed silently; it is the one open question in this file worth a reviewer's attention before generation. `frames` excludes `plant`, since a rooted, handless plant-frame body has no zombie-side existence in this game's fiction and the field itself does not exist for it. `roles` are the nine armour-class-bearing roles from classes.v1.json's `classLadders.armour` (identical list on both frames). Word table `Tin-clad / Iron-clad / Adamantine` reused verbatim from ssot-affixes.md §4.12's shipped sample — the one family in this group that document actually shows.

entries.name: Carapace
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. Same reasoning as `atom.plating` throughout — atom-family-library.md §3.1's `carapace | arm2/arm2Max` row, the same undocumented channel-pair `variants.generate` gap (definitions.md §1), the same resolution (author the single capacity channel `arm2Max` Flat and flag the current-field companion as a generator concern), the same zombie-only field fact (§4.1), and the same nine armour roles. No shipped word table exists for `carapace` specifically in ssot-affixes.md §4.12's sample (only `plating` is shown), so these words are minted fresh: a decaying-into-hardened-shell escalation that reads as this family's own register rather than reusing plating's metal-clad one, since the two families should not read as interchangeable synonyms.

entries.name: Bastion
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% more defense for the whole army
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `arm` (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies g.armour), word `hardening`. Fills the one primary-channel op this group leaves open: `defense` ships `Flat` (`warding`) and `Increased` (`resilience`) but no `More`, unlike `maxHp` (`vitality`/`fortitude`/`bulwark`) and `atk` (`might`/`ferocity`/`savagery`), which each complete the trio. classes.v1.json's design note is explicit that no `More`-op family ever appears on an implicit slate — `bulwark` and `savagery` are 'reserved for rolled affixes only' at rare tier — so this family follows the identical shape: rolled-only, never an implicit, and, like every other family in this group, legal exclusively on the commander `standard` role for the same G8 reason as `warding`/`resilience`, since it shares the same side-wide-cached `defense` channel. `powerBand: "low"` mirrors the Increased/More siblings elsewhere in this file and in the affix-family exemplar (`atom.elpw-amplify`) — a multiplicative rider earns its weight from stacking, not from a large band on its own. `StatComposer.ComposeDefense` folds `Increased` and `More` mods into the same percent pipeline (sum then product), so this is a real, distinct, executable composition today, not a quarantined one.

entries.name: Reinforced Plating
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `arm`, word `riveting`. `plating` (this file) is Flat-only, unlike every other primary channel with a shipped family, which leaves `arm1Max` without its `fortitude`-equivalent scaling sibling. This closes that gap the same way `fortitude` completes `vitality`: same channel (`arm1Max`, following this file's own resolution of the plating channel-pair question above), `op: Increased` instead of `Flat`. Thematically drawn from the Thorned Chassis register's own description ('scrap armor gets bolted onto a living stem') rather than plating's metal-clad word table, since a scaling rider should read as reinforcement work done to existing plating, not a second coat of the same metal. `roles`/`frames`/`side` identical to `atom.plating` — same zombie-only field, same nine armour roles.

entries.name: Reinforced Carapace
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `arm`, word `welding`. The `carapace` mirror of `atom.arm-riveting` — closes the same Flat-only gap on `arm2Max` that `arm-riveting` closes on `arm1Max`, for the identical reason (every other primary channel in the library ships with at least a Flat+Increased pair; `plating`/`carapace` did not). Same zombie-only field, same nine armour roles, same frames/side as `atom.carapace`. Kept as a distinct family from `arm-riveting` rather than one family spanning both channels, for the same reason `plating` and `carapace` are two families and not one: `effect_atom`'s unique key is `(family_id, tier, variant)`, and the two channels already belong to two separately-named shipped families, so their scaling siblings follow the same one-family-per-channel shape rather than reintroducing the channel-pair ambiguity flagged above.
